objective: Convert the current TRL 4-5 product experience into evidence-backed, externally sellable services without confusing prototypes with production controls.

operationalDefinition.label: 100_PERCENT_OPERATIONAL
operationalDefinition.rule: A product is operational only when every mandatory gate is PASS with current evidence; a percentage, demo, local test or roadmap entry is never sufficient.

financialGuardrails.rule: The contracted service must be fully covered without exceeding the customer tariff; activation is blocked when cost, margin or provider evidence is insufficient.

architecture.operatingModel: Modular core first; independently deployable Qu motors retain isolated repositories, services and approval gates when their runtime boundary is real.
forbiddenShortcuts: browser localStorage as authentication or entitlement
direct provider secrets or API calls from the public website
activation without order, entitlement and acceptance evidence
production or quantum-security claims based only on a prototype
unreviewed deployment or direct main-branch publication

phases.name: Product truth and portfolio freeze
exitCriteria: Authoritative catalog maps every offer to owner, provider, fulfillment mode, prerequisites and evidence state.
Provider capability and contract matrix distinguishes available, sandbox, negotiation and unsupported states.
Public claims, pricing and roadmap are aligned with verified capability states.
The first sellable slice is QuFense controlled beta; the provider-backed QuSOC assessment follows on the same transaction spine.

phases.name: Secure platform foundation
exitCriteria: QuIdentify uses server-issued OIDC/OAuth sessions, MFA and tenant-scoped RBAC.
Tenant isolation and resource authorization tests pass in CI.
QuVault stores references to an approved secret manager; no browser or repository secrets exist.
QuAudit records signed actor, tenant, policy, evidence and outcome events.
Logs, metrics, traces, backups and a tested restore path exist in a non-production environment.

phases.name: Commercial transaction spine
exitCriteria: Catalog, assessment, quote, acceptance, order, subscription and entitlement share one tenant-aware lifecycle.
QuCFA enforces provider cost, tariff hard cap and minimum 30 percent gross margin with deterministic tests.
QuPay verifies signed sandbox webhooks and records a durable payment ledger without storing card data.
Legal acceptance, product schedule, SLA and provider-specific dependencies are evidence-linked.
Refund, dispute, cancellation and failed-payment paths are tested.

phases.name: QuHub provisioning control plane
exitCriteria: A versioned provider-adapter contract supports validation, quote, provision, status, update, suspend, terminate and webhook normalization.
Every provider operation uses tenant scope, idempotency, redacted evidence, retry policy and dead-letter handling.
API_AUTO, HUMAN_ASSISTED and MANUAL_EXTERNAL fulfillment modes share one state machine.
Entitlements become active only after service-specific health and acceptance checks pass.
At least one sandbox adapter and one human-assisted fallback complete the full order-to-activation path.

phases.name: Customer activation and support
exitCriteria: QuDeploy exposes prerequisites, tasks, owner, progress, evidence, health and rollback per entitlement.
QuSupport operates severity, SLA clocks, escalation, provider handoff and customer verification.
The customer workspace exposes services, incidents, billing, documents, integrations and connector health by tenant and role.
Aggy provides evidence-cited guidance and never requests secrets in chat.
A supervised support drill restores a failed service and preserves the complete audit trail.

phases.name: First revenue-ready products
exitCriteria: QuFense controlled beta has independent security review, licensed scope, monitoring and tested recovery.
QuSOC and QuCISO complete one provider-backed alert-to-response workflow under an active agreement and SLA.
QuMarket completes one quote-to-cash-to-activation-to-support journey with a pilot tenant.
Actual provider cost, gross margin, activation time, intervention rate and support results are measured.
Pilot customer acceptance and rollback evidence are signed and retained.

phases.name: Graphene Ring expansion
exitCriteria: QuIntel and QuInfra each operate one contracted, monitored and supportable service slice.
Each new Graphene Ring offer reuses identity, commerce, entitlement, provisioning, evidence and support contracts.
QuLegal, QuLearn, QuTeach, QuAcademy and QuCertify workflows remain gated until their providers and legal roles are verified.
No new product enters sale without a complete operational scorecard and QuCFA economics.
Provider concentration, regional data, exit and substitution risks are documented.

phases.name: Production assurance and general availability
exitCriteria: Independent security assessment, incident exercise, backup restore and disaster-recovery objectives pass.
Production SLOs, capacity limits, on-call ownership and provider escalation paths are measured.
Privacy, DPA, subprocessor, SLA, insurance and jurisdictional reviews are approved for the launch markets.
All mandatory operational gates are PASS with non-expired evidence.
EDDIE VELASQUEZ ORTIZ explicitly approves production promotion after reviewing tests, risk, cost and rollback.

productWaves.purpose: Sell, activate and support one complete service
Expand only through the proven transaction spine

metrics: provisioning success and manual intervention rate
gross margin by product and tenant
first-response, resolution, reopen and customer verification
security incidents caused by platform change
agent approval, rejection and prohibited-action block rate
